title: Projectile Motion and Its Applications
notes: **Projectile:** any object thrown or launched into the air and then allowed to move under gravity alone.

**Key insight â€” independence of motions:** horizontal motion has zero acceleration ($a_x = 0$), so horizontal velocity is constant. Vertical motion has constant acceleration $g$ downward. The two motions are completely independent.

**Trajectory equation:** eliminating $t$ from $x = u\cos\theta \cdot t$ and $y = u\sin\theta \cdot t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ gives $y = x\tan\theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$, which is the equation of a parabola.
**Maximum height:** $H = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$. Reached when vertical velocity becomes zero.
**Time of flight:** $T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$. The projectile returns to the launch level when vertical displacement is zero.
**Horizontal range:** $R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$. The range is maximum when $\sin 2\theta = 1$, i.e., $\theta = 45\circ$.
**Applications:** sports (basketball shots, golf drives), military (artillery, rockets), and engineering (water fountains, ballistic trajectories) all rely on the same parabolic equations.
